text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- Serbian Deputy Interior Minister Radovan Stojicic shot dead by a masked gunman in a restaurant in central Belgrade.
- Yugoslavia forwarded a draft agreement on establishement of diplomatic relations with Bosnia-Herzegovina to members of the Bosnian presidency and Bosnian interior minister.

- President of the Serbs in Eastern Slavonian region in Croatia Goran Hadzic met Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic to discuss upcoming local elections. Yugoslavia has already launched initiatives for creating conditions for dual citizenship, statement said.
- The Serbs in Eastern Slavonia expect their Independent Democratic Serb Party (SDSS) to win in at least six municipalities in the region at the Sunday local elections.
- A protocol on technical and technological cooperation was signed between Yugoslav construction companies and French firm Freyssinet.
- A boiler breakdown halts production of thermo-electric power plant Plevlja, Montenegro.

- Serbian oil industry Naftna Industrija Serbije (NIS) says it is necessary to make preparations for reorganisation and ownership transformation so that it can be launched as soon as the law is passed.
- Serbia's province of Vojvodina will start afforestation of 90,000 hectares of land. Only 6.8 percent of the region's territory is under forests.
- The health sector is in a difficult financial situation and has to ask drug producers to supply products on credit, says Serbian Health Minister Leposava Milicevic.
- Third round of polio vaccination of children under five will start in central Serbia, Kosovo and Montenegro.
- Lack of financial discipline must be checked because it threatens to compromise regulatory functions of the central bank, says director of of Beobanka Zlatan Perucic.
NASA BORBA

- Participants of round table on Kosovo held in New York adopt joint statements and call for the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia to take part in the next meeting which will probably be held in Belgrade.
- Federal and Serbian budget revenues continue to be low.
- Belgrade city assembly appoints new managing boards in city firms.
- Serbian government agrees to speed up payment of teachers' February wages at a meeting with education trade unions.
- President of Association for Aid to Refugees in Yugoslavia Milorad Muraltovic warns about tragic situation of over 600,000 refugees in the country.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Yugoslavi will send observers for the local elections in Eastern Slavonia at the invitation of U.N. Administrator Jacques Klein.
- Reserves for soup kitchens can only last one more month if international organisations do not send more food, says Belgrade Red Cross.
BORBA
- Serbian government earmarks 375 million dinars for water management in 1997.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Federal government will introduce numeric markings on tax stamps put on cigarettes, coffee, alcoholic beverages and other goods for better control in an effort to stem smuggling.
- Kosovo Albanian separatists Thursday shot dead Ramiz Leku, an employee of the municipality of Glogovac.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA

- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic receives French Ambassador to Yugoslavia Stanislas Filiol who is in Podgorica to attend the opening of the French cultural centre. Filiol also received by Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.
- French cultural centre was opened by Filiol and Montenegirn culture Minister Goran Rakocevic.
- Montenegrin Information ministry rejected as "totally false" TV Serbia reports that its crew was harassed and forced to leave Montenegro.

- Montenegrin Health ministry and the National tourist organisation signed a $20 million deal with Swedish electrical equipment firm Electrolux which will provide equipment for Montenegrin hospitals while payments will be made through tourist barter arrangements for Swedish tourists. -- Belgrade Newsroom ++381 11 222 4254
